caption: The knob of a desk fan is turned from off to high, and the blades spin up to speed.

sa.check: A desk fan with a knob.
The knob is turned from off to high.
The blades spin up to speed.
The blades are still before the knob turns.
The order is still, turn, spinning.

pc.expect: The blades begin to turn as the knob leaves its off position, and only then, and speed up to a steady spin.
pc.fail: The knob is turned and the blades stay still to the end of the clip; or the blades spin before the knob moves; or the blades start with the knob untouched; or the blades spin at full speed from the first frame with the knob at off.

pc.expect: The spin builds one way from still to steady and holds while the knob stays at high; it does not stop or slow on its own.
pc.fail: The blades slow and stop with the knob still at high; or spin up and down repeatedly; or reverse direction; or the knob turns back by itself.

pc.expect: The blades spin about the hub as one piece with a smooth speed-up; the head may oscillate if built to.
pc.fail: The blades wobble off the hub; or move independently of each other; or the spin jumps abruptly between fast and still; or the whole fan spins on its base.

pc.expect: Light items in front of the fan flutter in the airflow once the blades spin and are still before.
pc.fail: Ribbons or paper flutter before the blades turn; or nothing in front moves while the fan runs; or the flutter blows toward the fan.
pc.precondition: Light items such as paper, ribbons or hair are in front of the fan.

pc.expect: One fan with a fixed number of blades; the fan stays on the desk; the hand passes through nothing.
pc.fail: Blades appear or vanish; or the fan duplicates; or the fan lifts off the desk; or the hand passes through the cage.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The fan's colour, the cage pattern and the desk stay the same.
pc.fail: The fan changes colour; or the cage pattern changes; or items on the desk rearrange.
